summary.name: Computer numerical control
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining computer numerical control (CNC), the computer-driven automation of machine tools using G-code and M-code programs.
use_cases: comparing open-loop and closed-loop machine control
reviewing CNC crash and backlash risks
summary.what_it_does: The page describes CNC as the automated control of machine tools by a computer, evolved from punched-tape numerical control. It explains the CAD to CAM to post-processor workflow that turns a part design into machine instructions. It covers positioning with open-loop and closed-loop systems, Cartesian coordinates, and collision and backlash issues. It lists common G-code and M-code commands with a sample program, and describes CNC mills, lathes, plasma cutters, EDM, waterjet cutters and punch presses.
notable: Explains G-code and M-code with a worked coding example
Covers open-loop vs closed-loop control and stepper slip/crash detection
Lists CNC machine types and many CNC-variant tools
caveats: Describes general concepts rather than a software tool; no software platforms are named
Some sections lack citations, and parts of the page are flagged as needing citation
